Olivia —

Appreciate the quick turnaround. Draft numbers below and attaching a workbook with the detail.

Summary (committed reserved slots):
- Baseline reserved: 48 GPU-hours/day (equivalent to 3 x large reserved slots given Acme model mix)
- Expected steady token throughput: 1.2M tokens/day (peak 1.9M)
- Recommended launch buffer: +35% reserved capacity for first 30 days (handles 95th percentile of observed spikes in pilots)
- Burst credit guidance: 20% of daily baseline available as on-demand burst (estimated cost impact shown in workbook)

Run-of-show for PO/Launch:
1) Sign PO with the baseline reserved quantities (48 GPU-hrs/day) — expected start 2026-11-01
2) Redwood ops will pre-warm KV caches and pin model version for 48 hours prior to go-live
3) Monitor first 7 days via Console; auto-scaling disabled for reserved slots unless both parties agree
4) After day 30, we recommend re-evaluating steady-state; refunds/credits subject to contract terms

Attaching: runway_buffer_calcs.xlsx

Next steps: Can your finance lead confirm acceptable buffer % and whether they prefer buffer as part of the committed monthly invoice or billed as on-demand burst? If you can loop in Finance procurement contact I can craft the final PO language.

Thanks,
Laura
Laura Bennett
Director, Sales Operations
Redwood Inference

Olivia — quick clarifying note from Sales-side assumptions: 

- We scoped 3 reserved slots mapped to customer's model mix (2 large LLM instances + 1 medium for async workloads)
- If Acme wants buffer included in monthly commit, the commitment steps up to 65 GPU-hrs/day (same discount tiers apply)
- Alternatively, we can keep baseline 48 and allow burst to 58 via on-demand; finance often prefers not to increase committed since it affects forecasted run-rates

Ben from FinOps (cc'd) — any quick guidance on what procurement teams typically accept? Grace from Infra — can you confirm we can hold 2 standby spot-capable nodes for rapid scaling during launch week?

Marcus
Associate VP, Sales
From: ben_carter@redwood.ai
To: marcus_lin@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai, Olivia Hart <olivia@acme.ai>
Cc: grace_oconnor@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-10-11T15:47:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Redwood Dedicated ask: final capacity numbers before PO

Looping Finance — short answer:

- Procurement teams usually prefer buffer baked into the commit if they need predictable billing and want to avoid overage charges; that converts to a higher committed ARR which may need procurement sign-off earlier.
- If Acme needs flexibility, we can do a hybrid: 48 base committed + 30% reserved buffer line-item that is cancellable after 60 days with 30-day notice (allows Acme to de-risk)
- Please note: refunds on committed reductions are pro-rated and subject to minimum term in contract.

Grace — infra confirmation?

Ben
Head of Finance Operations
